source.quote: One major change is that it's now a ESM only package

tasks.reasoning:
The repo uses node-fetch for its only Riot HTTP call, but the usage map does not record the installed node-fetch version. node-fetch 3.0.0 is ESM-only, so require() breaks. That matters if the TypeScript/serverless build compiles to CommonJS. Today it only bites if the repo is on 3.x with CJS output, or when it upgrades. The migration agent should check the node-fetch version in package.json/package-lock.json and the tsconfig module target. If the version is <3, either stay on the 2.x line (no change needed) or replace node-fetch with Node 18+ global fetch. If it is 1.x, also apply the 2.0 upgrade guide. Low urgency: there is no deadline and no forced breakage unless the dependency is bumped.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- riot:node-fetch-2-0-0 (sdk-major): node-fetch (npm) 2.0.0 major release with breaking changes from 1.x; see upgrade guide. Moving node-fetch to 3.x crosses the 2.0.0 major as well. If the repo is still on 1.x, the 2.0 upgrade-guide changes (Headers/Response behaviour, body handling) get handled in the same edit to src/libs/riotApi.ts. If it is already on 2.x, nothing extra is needed.
  Source: https://api.github.com/repos/node-fetch/node-fetch/releases?per_page=100
  "This is a major release. See [upgrade guide](https://github.com/bitinn/node-fetch/blob/master/UPGRADE-GUIDE.md) on how to upgrade from v1.x"

callSites.why: The Riot summoner-v4 call is made with node-fetch, which appears in this usage's packages. Moving to node-fetch 3.x means the import must work with an ESM-only package. Either the build must emit ESM / use dynamic import(), or the call should move to Node's built-in global fetch.

record.prBody:
## node-fetch (npm) 3.0.0 is ESM only; require() no longer works [Verified]

### Change

The repo was already on node-fetch 3.3.0 (ESM-only) while the code compiles to CommonJS. I removed the node-fetch import from src/libs/riotApi.ts and uninstalled the package. The code now uses Node's global fetch (Node >=18.12.1 in engines, nodejs18.x runtime). I bumped @types/node to ^18.19.0 so `fetch` type-checks. The 2.0.0 upgrade guide needed nothing, since the repo was never on 1.x.

Files touched:
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `src/libs/riotApi.ts`
- `test/no-node-fetch.test.mjs`

### Why

node-fetch 3 is ESM-only and require() no longer works with it. Dropping it for global fetch removes that risk.

> One major change is that it's now a ESM only package

Source: https://api.github.com/repos/node-fetch/node-fetch/releases?per_page=100

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | fail (3) | fail (1) | 0 |
| no-node-fetch | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- no-node-fetch, added by the agent: `node test/no-node-fetch.test.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `no-node-fetch`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Bundling and deploy with serverless were not run.
- The Riot call was not exercised at runtime. Only a static test covers the change.
- Typecheck still has one error that was already there, in @serverless/typescript. The two node-fetch and formdata-polyfill type errors from the baseline are gone.
- typecheck was already failing before the change and still fails.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- HTTP now goes through Node's built-in fetch (undici) instead of node-fetch. The request and the res.json() handling are the same.
- @types/node bumped from 18.11 to 18.19 in devDependencies.

---

preparation.reasoning: The only check is `tsc --noEmit`. The repo has no codegen, no workspace packages and no prepare/postinstall scripts that the type check depends on. Dependencies and types are already installed, so no setup is needed.

review.summary: Dropping node-fetch for Node 18's global fetch is a reasonable fix for the ESM-only change. `src/libs/riotApi.ts` is the only importer shown, and the call shape (URL plus headers, then `res.json()`) works the same with native fetch. The grade is the problem: typecheck still fails after the change (1 error), so 'verified' isn't supported by the checks. The new test also only proves that the CI Node has global fetch, not that the deployed Lambda runtime does.

concerns.issue: Typecheck still fails after the change (3 errors down to 1), and the PR doesn't say which error remains. It could be the global `fetch` in this file not resolving, for example if tsconfig `lib` lacks DOM and @types/node 18.19 globals aren't picked up. If so, the migrated call site doesn't compile. A 'verified' grade with a failing typecheck doesn't match the checks.

Global fetch only exists at runtime on Node 18+. `package.json` has `engines >=18.12.1`, but the Lambda `provider.runtime` (and any esbuild `target`) in `serverless.ts` isn't shown. If it is `nodejs16.x` or lower, `fetchSummoner` will throw `ReferenceError: fetch is not defined` in production. The `globalThis.fetch` assertion in `test/no-node-fetch.test.mjs` runs on the CI Node, not the Lambda runtime.

`@types/node` goes from ^18.11.11 to ^18.19.130, pulling in `undici-types`. This is presumably to get global fetch typings, so it's justified, but it is a wider type surface change than the API change strictly forces.

This is a grep-style test: it checks file text and package.json, not behaviour. Nothing exercises `fetchSummoner` (no mocked fetch, no live call to Riot). Behaviour differences between native fetch and node-fetch, such as error types on network failure ('fetch failed' TypeError), are untested.

Pre-existing and not caused by this PR: `name` is interpolated into the URL without `encodeURIComponent`. The two fetch implementations may handle unencoded spaces and unicode summoner names differently, so worth checking now.

checkFirst: Read the one remaining typecheck error after the change and confirm it isn't in src/libs/riotApi.ts (global fetch/Response types).
Check serverless.ts provider.runtime and the esbuild target are nodejs18.x or later so global fetch exists in Lambda.
Grep the rest of src/ for any other 'node-fetch' imports or node-fetch-specific types (e.g. RequestInit from node-fetch).
Do a smoke call of fetchSummoner (mocked or against Riot) to confirm headers and json parsing behave the same.
